_readme: Ground truth for the form-finding evaluation. Each entry names a movement by
opus and movement number -- never by work id, which is assigned at ingest and
changes when the corpus is rebuilt -- and every bar number below is a PRINTED
bar number, the kind a performer reads and the kind the LLM must cite.
Two different bars are recorded for the return of the opening material and the
distinction matters, because conflating them would let the harness score a
correct answer as wrong:
recapitulation  -- where published analysis puts the start of the recap.
literal_return  -- where note-for-note correspondence with the exposition
actually begins in this encoding.
They coincide when Beethoven brings the theme back unaltered and diverge when
he recomposes its first bars: the Waldstein's recapitulation is at m. 156 but
its literal correspondence with m. 3 does not begin until m. 160. A symbolic
matcher can only ever find the second. `literal_return` is therefore what the
pipeline is scored against, and it is verified rather than remembered -- every
value carries a `verified` score, the varies/repeats confidence measured over
an 8-bar window between it and `exposition_start`. `recapitulation` is recorded
alongside it so the gap between what is findable and what a musician would say
stays visible instead of being quietly defined away.
A null `literal_return` is a real negative, not missing data: no window in the
movement matches the opening well enough to be called a return.

movements.notes: Theme returns unaltered; recapitulation and literal return coincide.
Three recomposed bars lead into the literal return.
Grave introduction mm. 1-10; the Allegro exposition proper begins at m. 11, and the recapitulation re-enters two bars before correspondence resumes.
Arpeggio theme returns at pitch; the second group is what moves up a fourth.
The recapitulation opens with the Largo arpeggio and recitative; the Allegro material only lines up again eight bars later.
Recapitulation is recomposed for four bars before mm. 3ff resume verbatim.
Known negative. The theme returns over a drumming tonic pedal that the exposition does not have, so no window reaches a return threshold. Also the movement with no notated exposition repeat.
Known negative. The movement whose second section repeats rather than its first.
Known negative. Maestoso introduction mm. 1-18; the fugal subject is developed continuously rather than restated, which is what makes the return hard to find.
